concepts_addressed: Geographic Expansion Sequence: Dominate Local, Then Expand

frameworks.name: Drop-Servicing Niche Selection Filter
frameworks.definition: Three criteria that make a niche viable for a remote drop-servicing business: (1) high average ticket (targeting ~$7,500/job), (2) low Google Map Pack competition (few reviews, no keyword-optimized names), (3) strong local search volume sufficient to generate required lead flow.

frameworks.name: Keyword-Optimized Google Business Profile Ranking Method
frameworks.definition: A two-factor ranking formula for Google Map Pack: (1) include the service keyword and city name verbatim in the business profile name, and (2) accumulate more high-star reviews than competitors. Whichever profile best matches the search query's exact terms ranks first regardless of age.

examples.text: A student named Sammy joined Eric's program on May 8th and within 20 days closed his first job in the landscaping niche for $9,500, plus several smaller jobs. Sammy is operating a drop-servicing landscaping business, confirming that the landscaping niche can produce high-ticket closes quickly for a new entrant.

A student named Cole sent out a quote for $300,000 on a landscaping job through the drop-servicing model. This illustrates that landscaping is not capped at $7,500/job — some projects run into hundreds of thousands of dollars, making the niche's upside substantially larger than the conservative $7,500 average ticket the speaker uses in his profit math.

A student named Walker accumulated only four reviews on his Google Business Profile but was getting multiple inbound leads per day. This illustrates the speaker's claim that in low-competition niches, even a sparse profile with correct keyword optimization and a handful of reviews generates consistent lead flow without needing hundreds of reviews.

An unidentified student in Eric's group was operating a drop-servicing asphalt business with only three reviews on a single Google Business Profile and was getting leads every single day. The speaker cited this as evidence that the asphalt niche in cities like Atlanta requires minimal review accumulation to generate qualified inbound leads.

In Peterborough, Ontario, the speaker searched 'Electrician Peterborough' and found competitor 'Lancer Electric' ranked with a 4.6-star rating and 107 reviews, while a competitor with only 15 reviews ranked above Lancer because the 15-review profile contained the exact search phrase 'electrician Peterborough' in its business name. This concrete comparison illustrates the keyword-name ranking mechanism: name relevance outweighs review count in the Google Map Pack when the name contains the exact search query.

Eric described his own plumbing Google Business Profile in Newmarket, Ontario which has 116 reviews and consistently generates approximately 80 leads per month — documented as 46 calls and 124 website clicks in April alone. He used this profile as the baseline to establish that one profile can provide roughly 80 leads/month, requiring only two such profiles to hit the 120-lead threshold for $50,000/month profit.

practices.text: To acquire reviews quickly for a new Google Business Profile, post in local Facebook groups asking people to leave a review, ask friends and family, and approach strangers at a local coffee shop (e.g., buy everyone in line a coffee and ask them to review your business). This can yield 50+ reviews in approximately 30 minutes of effort.

When selecting a city for a drop-servicing niche, use a keyword research tool (e.g., SEMrush free tier via Gmail account rotation) to check monthly search volume for the target service + city phrase, then cross-reference with the Google Map Pack to count competitor reviews and check whether any top-3 profiles have the service keyword and city name in their business name.

When creating a new Google Business Profile for a local service niche, include both the service keyword and the city name verbatim in the business profile name (e.g., 'Stucco Phoenix' or 'Landscaping Los Angeles') to maximize name-relevance matching in Google's Map Pack algorithm.

For drop-servicing businesses targeting $50,000/month profit, begin with landscaping, asphalt/paving, stucco, or masonry rather than HVAC or electrical in major metros, because competition review counts are far lower (10-43 reviews vs. 3,000-5,000 reviews) while ticket sizes remain in the same $2,500-$8,000+ range.
